$comment: The releases this project measures itself against, and the facts that identify them.
Read by the `Reference releases are intact` step in release-dmg.yml, which fails the
build if any of these tags disappears or moves to a different commit.
GitHub-side tag protection became available when this repository was made public on
2026-08-17 — rulesets need Pro or a public repository, and it is now the latter. This
check is kept alongside rather than replaced by one: a ruleset can stop a tag being
deleted, but it does not record which commit the tag is supposed to point at, nor the
digest of the artifact that was published from it. Those are the facts a fallback point
is actually made of, and they live here.
Five references. v1.0.5 is the floor, v1.0.9 closes the 1.x line, v2.5.11 and v2.6.1
are earlier 2.x releases, and v2.6.2 is the current one, published on 2026-09-29. A release
cannot record itself — the commit it names is the commit that carries it, and no file
can contain its own hash — so each entry here is added by the commit after the release
it describes.
v2.6.2 was added beside v2.6.1 on 2026-09-29, not in its place, under the rule of
2026-09-23. v2.6.1 replaced v2.6.0 by the owner's decision of 2026-09-26: v2.6.0 was withdrawn —
release, tag and DMG — and v2.5.11 stays, as it did when v2.6.0 was published on
2026-09-23, the first release since 2026-08-30 not to displace the one before it. Before
that the list was kept at three, and the release a new one replaced was withdrawn:
v2.5.10 on 2026-09-22, v2.5.9 on 2026-09-20, hours after it was published, v2.5.8
earlier that day, v2.5.7 on 2026-09-13, v2.5.6 earlier the same day, v2.5.5 on
reference cannot be re-cut, so the work that follows one takes a number of its own.
Whether a new release retires anything is a decision rather than a consequence of
publishing.
Adding or changing any value below is a deliberate act and shows up in the diff as one.

references.why: First release of the numbering that survives; everything before it was withdrawn.
The second reference: credits the corpus authors, bounds a download that had nothing but the disk to stop it, and is the recent state to fall back to rather than the floor.

The third reference, kept by v2.6.0 and again by v2.6.1. It replaced v2.5.10, and unlike that one it carries code: the inventory's search field is labelled in English, a CTH group is one run even when its labels share a number, a dropped BOM is counted under DROP_BOM, and two cache tests no longer leave a working directory in TMPDIR. The package it builds hashes to dfe12b37…adff over 23 940 files, the byte mirror to the unchanged 7cfcdce4…35d0 over 23 936 documents in 663 folders. It is the first release whose binary is reproducible across machines: the application the runner built, 4e2786bc…a594, is byte-for-byte the one the owner's machine builds from the same commit, because the release build remaps the building machine's paths, keeps the debug map out of LC_UUID, and holds Xcode 15.2 (SDK 14.2) and Node 22.23.2 on both sides. Revisions 80 and 81.

The fourth reference, in the place of v2.6.0, withdrawn the same day by the owner's decision, and kept by v2.6.2. It publishes into a folder under a flock lock and says when it waits for another run; checks the staged copy against the published one before the reader's goes; takes the proxy from the environment and goes direct, saying so, when it cannot use it; ends a question to Zenodo behind a silent proxy by its own deadline, and names an expired deadline as one; refuses two CTH groups the disk would file as one folder and names their code points when only Unicode form differs; refuses in Russian in the console; reads the archive through an 8 KiB buffer, 10.8 % fewer instructions than 256 KiB. The package it builds hashes to 83392544…3dc99 over 23 941 files, the byte mirror to the unchanged 7cfcdce4…35d0. The application the runner built, 6976fbf2…a5e7, is byte-for-byte the one the release gate built twice on the owner's machine. Revisions 90–99.

The current release and the fifth reference, beside v2.6.1. A run that waits through many holders of the publish lock takes the lock itself instead of publishing beside another run; in 2.6.1 the race was counted as unstable inode numbers (d18e1dd, simplified in ccd122a). Tauri 2.11.6 binds channel data and large invoke replies to the webview they were made for, GHSA-w28w-mhc8-qvjv; Aruna has one webview, so there was no direct exposure. The package it builds hashes to the unchanged 83392544…3dc99 over 23 941 files, the byte mirror to 7cfcdce4…35d0. The application the runner built, 509c98d8…ff3b, is byte-for-byte the one the release gate built twice on the owner's machine from 55c2df9; the tag's commit differs from it only in documents. Revisions 105–112.
